discovery: Discovery of intrinsic magnetism in atomically thin van der Waals crystals
motivation: In 2017 Xu, Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers showed layer-dependent ferromagnetism in monolayer CrI3, and Zhang and co-workers showed ferromagnetism in few-layer Cr2Ge2Te6. Mermin-Wagner physics had long suggested that long-range magnetic order in two dimensions was fragile, and these experiments showed that magnetic anisotropy stabilizes it down to single atomic layers. The discovery opened a new class of quantum materials. Since then, groups have shown electrically switchable magnetism, giant tunneling magnetoresistance in spin-filter junctions, layered antiferromagnets whose magnetic and optical properties can be engineered, and magnon and exciton physics that can be probed and driven by light. Two-dimensional magnets now underpin work on multiferroics, magnetoelectric coupling, and moire magnetism. Their stacking with other van der Waals materials makes them a platform for spintronics and for controlling quantum phases at the atomic limit.
